captive_summary: Futtsu LNG Terminal is JERA's LNG base embedded within the giant Futtsu Thermal Power Station complex (~5,160-5,334 MW). TEPCO/JERA's official regulatory capacity-disclosure filing lists the base's full equipment as LNG tanks (10 tanks, 1.11 million kL) plus ORV vaporizers and a 熱調設備 (heat-conditioning system) only — no separate generation plant. Gas from the base fuels Futtsu itself and is piped onward to other Keiyo/Keihin-side plants via the East-West interconnection gas pipeline — the base is auxiliary infrastructure of the power station, not the reverse.
confirmed_how: JERA's mandatory 液化ガス貯蔵設備の容量等の公表 filing itemizes the Futtsu LNG base's equipment (tanks, ORV vaporizers, heat-conditioning) with no boiler/turbine/engine/generator line item. This is a 'captive to WHOM' case in the opposite sense from most: the LNG base sits physically inside the Futtsu power station's site and draws station-service power from Futtsu itself (the primary generating asset), rather than having any separate captive plant of its own.

hardware_summary: 2x MHIET KU30GA natural gas engines, 5,500 kW each (11,000 kW / 11 MW total generation capacity), gas-engine cogeneration installed 2004; retrofitted in 2018 with Miller-cycle combustion and a switch from micro-pilot-oil ignition to spark ignition, further reducing residual liquid-fuel dependence.

MHIET's 2018 retrofit release independently confirms the engine model (KU30GA) and describes converting the ignition system away from oil-pilot ignition toward spark ignition — corroborating gas, not diesel/oil, as the operating fuel.
captive_summary: Hiroshima Gas installed an 11,000 kW (2x 5,500 kW) natural-gas-engine cogeneration plant at its Hatsukaichi factory in 2004 specifically to power the LNG terminal's own refrigeration/vaporization load, with waste heat recovered as hot water for LNG vaporization (cutting vaporization fuel gas use by ~60% per the announcement) and surplus power (~10,000 kW) wheeled to the grid for wholesale sale. This is on-site gas-fired electricity generation whose primary purpose is powering the terminal — a captive, partially-exporting plant, and stays green even with the grid-export component per SOP.
